sampling_model.design: Two-arm baseline randomized trial with fixed switch time \(k\), terminal horizon \(K\), and no observed cross-arm switching.
sampling_model.units: Independent trial participants with fixed finite recurrent-event and death histories under the superpopulation law \(\mathsf P\).
sampling_model.treatment: Baseline assignment \(R\in\{0,1\}\); candidate regimes retain intensive treatment before \(k\) and switch survivors with \(B\ge m\) to standard treatment.
sampling_model.overlap: Positive baseline assignment and positive arm-specific censoring continuation on every positive-probability factual at-risk history through \(K\); no positivity is required for the unsupported post-landmark switch.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite vectors \((r_{bt},q_w)\) are identified under factual-arm sequential coarsening at random and estimated with censoring adjustment; the open inference question asks for uniformly valid efficient scores and cross-fitting at Hall and policy ties.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper identifies relevant marginal residual-count laws under no carry-over and gives pointwise bounds for an unsupported one-time switch.
The paper characterizes atom-sensitive sharp bounds for the distribution of an unrestricted sum with fixed marginals.

Theorem 4 characterizes nonempty fixed-margin staircase transportation classes by critical-position inequalities, and Section 3 gives constructions; Theorem 1 is the general arbitrary-pattern \((R,S)\)-support antecedent.
The paper gives greedy optimization results for staircase transportation problems with structured rewards.
The paper shows that the joint geometry of partially identified treatment payoffs governs minimax-regret rules and their randomization.
The paper formulates compatibility of causal marginal models with a single global structural causal model.
The paper obtains confidence regions for identified sets by inverting criterion functions under moment equalities and inequalities.
The paper develops regularized support-function inference for polygonal affine identified sets with changing active faces.

body.tldr: A randomized recurrent-event trial identifies separately capped baseline and residual marginals for a hypothetical switch while leaving their dependence unknown; the primitive recurrent-event paths remain raw and unbounded. The externally prespecified sensitivity restriction \(B+W\le H\) turns that ambiguity into a Ferrers transport problem and is not implied by individual capping. Dahl2008, Theorem 4, supplies the reindexed antidiagonal feasibility criterion. The novel kernel derives atom-correct capped endpoints, proves that every feasible triple coupling has an observed-law-preserving raw-path FFRCISTG realization under factual-arm sequential censoring, identifies the complete common-coupling threshold-value image, and computes exact minimax regret from signed pairwise differences. On a relatively open cap-three family, the shared-law payoff set strictly tightens threshold-wise scalar bounds and reverses their minimax choice. A perspective confidence-polytope inversion covers the whole value set and every minimax threshold at Hall and policy ties; efficient inference under sequential coarsening remains the first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: The closest recurrent-event switching analysis supplies a no-carry-over condition and scalar sharp bounds one threshold at a time. Dahl2008, Theorem 4, separately settles staircase fixed-margin feasibility. Neither line identifies atom-correct capped threshold endpoints, verifies that every compatible summary coupling lifts to an observed-law-preserving recurrent-event response tree under factual-arm censoring, preserves one latent law across a threshold menu, or derives the resulting strict minimax-regret separation and optimizer coverage.
project_justification.niche: An externally prespecified joint-capacity sensitivity restriction on two separately capped summaries creates nested antidiagonal support without globally bounding the underlying recurrent-event paths. The attributed staircase feasibility result in Dahl2008, Theorem 4, then becomes an input to a causal sharpness and joint-decision problem rather than the source of novelty.
project_justification.fill: The formal kernel combines the reindexed feasibility certificate from Dahl2008, Theorem 4, with an explicit raw-path causal lift, atom-correct closed-form endpoints, a common-coupling value polytope, exact shared-law regret with signed pairwise differences, a strict open-family comparison with scalar-bound decisions, a specialized support oracle, and simultaneous confidence-set inversion.

body.related_work: JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 Assumption 1 supplies the no-carry-over template specialized here to separately capped post-landmark increments; its Proposition 1 and decision section supply threshold-wise scalar sharp bounds and regime logic. Combining that capped specialization with an independently prespecified joint-capacity sensitivity restriction creates the setting for the new backward-deficit endpoints, observed-law-preserving lift, common-coupling payoff image, and strict open-family regret separation. Strassen1965 gives the general support-constrained coupling principle. More directly, Dahl2008, Theorem 4 and Section 3, already characterize fixed-margin staircase feasibility and constructions; Theorem 1 is the general arbitrary-pattern \((R,S)\)-support antecedent. After reversing the row order, the antidiagonal Hall criterion in this core is exactly the published Theorem 4 specialization and is not claimed as new. ZhangRichardson2025 explains why weak and strict distribution events require separate care for discrete sums and informs the atom-correct endpoint analysis. HoffmanVeinott1993 informs the staircase greedy argument under superadditive rewards; the support oracle here is a specialized exchange result for threshold-induced row coefficients of arbitrary sign and is not presented as freestanding algorithmic novelty. RichardsonRobins2013 provides the FFRCISTG semantics, and GreseleEtAl2022 frames the local-to-global causal-marginal obstruction addressed by the raw-path response-tree lift. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026 shows why joint payoff geometry matters for regret, whereas the present payoff set is generated by one capped transport law rather than a Gaussian reduced-form experiment. ChernozhukovHongTamer2007, AndrewsSoares2010, and Gafarov2025 inform confidence inversion at binding inequalities and changing faces. BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023, Proposition 1 and Corollary 1, distinguishes full from sequential coarsening at random and supports identification from factual-arm at-risk histories; its efficiency-bound and multiply robust estimation results inform the open semiparametric inference question.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The primitive counts are raw, nonnegative-integer-valued, and not globally bounded by \(H\). The condition \(B+W\le H\) constrains one switched counterfactual branch after separately capping its prefix burden and residual increment; it is a substantive shape restriction, not a loss normalization and not a consequence of the response-tree universe. A finite-reserve mechanism gives a concrete compatible class, but no such mechanism has been established for SPRINT. Dahl's feasibility criterion can reject a proposed sensitivity cap statistically, but it cannot establish clinical credibility. The response-tree theorem preserves only the original arm-specific sequential censoring law on factual at-risk histories; independence between censoring and the entire cross-world response tree is neither assumed nor produced. Assigning independent errors to all branches would strengthen FFRCISTG to an NPSEM model and would not establish the stated claim. Two executable diagnostics remain part of the audit rather than proposed results. The endpoint boundary test sets \(H=3\), \(m=1\), \(p_1=1\), and \(q_2=1\); the unique plan \(x_{1,2}=1\) gives \(Z_{m,L_m}^{+}=a_m=1\) and the upper endpoint \(2\). The signed-regret test sets \(H=2\), \(\pi=1\), \(\mathcal M=\{1,2\}\), \(p_1=1\), \(q_0=1\), and \(\mu_1=1\); the unique plan gives \(D_{12}=-1\) and \(R_1=0\), so implementations must not clip off-diagonal pairwise differences before maximizing over comparators.
body.honest_scope: The atom-correct endpoint consequences, raw-path causal lift under factual-arm sequential censoring, common-law value and regret characterization, nondegenerate regret separation, rational witness, and confidence inversion are to be proved. The antidiagonal Hall criterion is used solely as the reindexed feasibility support supplied by Dahl2008, Theorem 4, rather than proposed as a transportation theorem. The endpoint boundary and signed-regret calculations in the technical diagnostic are executable tests, not theorem contributions. Uniform semiparametric inference under sequential coarsening at random is deliberately open. When the joint-capacity restriction is removed and \(\mathcal M=\{m\}\), the endpoint problem reverts to unrestricted fixed-marginal bounds of the kind used by JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 and clarified by ZhangRichardson2025; this unrestricted reduction is contextual rather than a claim that the displayed capped formula remains unchanged after deleting its support. SPRINT is only a conditional capped-loss consumer: a mechanism and cap must be justified externally and prespecified at \(k=300\); the application is rejected if no credible joint-capacity interpretation exists or the censoring-adjusted Hall confidence system is infeasible.
